newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity bond chief consolidates munis in N.H.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity bond chief consolidates munis in N.H.

text.p: Fidelity Investments will be consolidating its municipal bond operations in Merrimack, New Hampshire, as the nation's largest mutual fund company adopts the team approach to investing, Fred Henning head of Fidelity's fixed income unit said Monday.
Fidelity has about $30 billion in municipals and despite the recent problems in the market, Henning remains upbeat about its prospects.

"No matter what they do, there will always be a need for the political subdivisions (to issue bonds) whether it's taxable or tax-exempt," he said, noting the increase in paper issues not subject to alternate minimum tax.
Fidelity will be moving its 15 muni analysts from Dallas and Boston to Merrimack, N.H., the site of a former Digital Equipment Corp location.

"It will be even more powerful," Henning said of the muni group. "We have four folks that do exclusive municpal quantitative research. We have full time counsel. What we try to do is understand what we're buying. Because if you understand what you buy, there is less risk."
Fidelity has funds covering California, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Connecticut.
